subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction?
options: Particles move faster and collide more often with more energy
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more energy, so they collide more frequently and more energetically.

questions.q: Which of these is an endothermic process?
questions.explain: Thermal decomposition takes in energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: Which method could be used to measure the rate of a reaction that produces a gas?
options: Measuring the colour of the flask
Measuring the volume of gas collected over time
questions.explain: Collecting and measuring the volume of gas produced over time gives the rate.

questions.q: Is bond making endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Forming new bonds releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: Which ion do all acids release when dissolved in water?
questions.explain: Acids are substances that release hydrogen ions (H⁺) in aqueous solution.

questions.q: Why does a non-rechargeable battery eventually stop working?
options: One of the reactants is used up
questions.explain: In a non-rechargeable cell the reaction stops once one of the reactants is used up.

questions.q: When making a soluble salt from an insoluble base and acid, why is excess base added?
options: To ensure all the acid is neutralised
questions.explain: Excess insoluble base guarantees all the acid reacts; the leftover solid is then filtered off.

questions.q: On a reaction profile, the activation energy is:
options: The minimum energy needed to start the reaction
The energy of the products only
The energy difference between reactants and products
questions.explain: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for reactant particles to react, shown as the hump on the profile.

questions.q: When citric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, the temperature falls. This reaction is:
questions.explain: The temperature drop shows energy is taken in, so the reaction is endothermic.

questions.q: Two acids have the same concentration but acid X has a lower pH than acid Y. What can you conclude?
options: Acid Y is a stronger acid
Acid X is a stronger acid
questions.explain: At equal concentration, the acid that ionises more (lower pH) is the stronger acid.

questions.q: Which salt is formed when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts, so sodium chloride is formed.

questions.q: A reaction is exothermic overall when:
options: More energy is released making bonds than absorbed breaking bonds
Equal energy is absorbed and released
More energy is absorbed breaking bonds than released making bonds
questions.explain: If bond-making releases more energy than bond-breaking absorbs, the reaction is exothermic overall.
